candidate_relations.label: Somatoform Disorder
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture—repeated episodes with no objective findings, normal tryptase during acute events, no laryngoscopic edema, and a psychiatric background with deliberate self-administration of epinephrine—points to intentional symptom fabrication (factitious disorder) rather than unconscious somatization. Somatoform disorder is an incompatible subtype because it lacks the volitional component central to the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Somatoform/functional disorder involves unconscious symptom production, whereas factitious disorder requires intentional feigning or induction of symptoms for sick-role benefit

candidate_relations.label: Factitious disorder imposed on self, recurrent
candidate_relations.reason: All required components are present: factitious disorder (intentional symptom production for sick-role benefit) imposed on self (the patient herself), with recurrent episodes confirmed by seven similar PICU admissions. The added specifiers are clinically supported and do not introduce incompatible elements.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Matches the reference diagnosis; 'imposed on self' and 'recurrent' are consistent qualifiers that do not conflict with the benchmark

case_quality_flags: Psychiatric comorbidities (MDD, suicidal ideation, auditory hallucinations, eating disorder) strongly support factitious disorder over organic allergy
Normal serial tryptase, negative allergy workup, and absence of objective edema on laryngoscopy are key discriminating findings
